wikivoyage.text:
Eat:
Portuguese cuisine evolved from hearty peasant food drawn from the land and abundant seafood found in the country's lengthy coast with the cows, pigs and goats raised on the limited grazing land of its interior. From these humble origins, spices and condiments brought back to the country during the exploration and colonisation of South America, Africa, the East Indies and the Far East, contributed to the development of what become regarded as 'typical' Portuguese cuisine which inherently, also helped shape the cuisine in the regions under Portuguese influence, from Brazil and Cape Verde to Thailand and Japan. Today, traditional Portuguese cuisine is served alongside the latest trendy and fusion cuisine styles. Several establishments have been awarded Michelin stars.

Soup is an essential first course of a Portuguese meal. The most popular is the Minho speciality, caldo verde, made from kale, potatoes and spiced smoked sausage.

You will see another Portuguese staple bacalhau (salt cod) everywhere. Locals will tell you that there are as many ways to cook this revered dish as there are days in the year, or even more.

The most common of Portugal's delicious fish (peixe) dishes revolve around sole (linguado) and sardines (sardinha) although salmon (salmão) and trout (truta) are also featured heavily, not mentioning the more traditional mackerel (carapau), whiting (pescada), rock bass (robalo), tuna (atum), frog fish (tamboril) and a variety of turbot (cherne).

In most places you will easily find fresh seafood: lobster (lagosta), crab (caranguejo), lavagante, mussels (mexilhões), cockles (vieiras), oysters (ostras), clam (amêijoas), goose barnacles (perceves).

A peculiarity of Portuguese cuisine is the love of rice and rice-based dishes and desserts, a fondness perhaps grown from the Portuguese travels to the East. Among the most popular rice dishes are "Arroz à Bulhão Pato", essentially a juicy rice and clam dish. Another famous rice dish, "Arroz de Cabidela" consisting of a saucy dish made with rice, chicken and its blood. Besides those already mentioned, there are many varieties of rice-based specialities, such as frog fish rice, octopus rice, duck rice and seafood rice.

Depending on how touristy the area you are in, you'll see grills, thick with the smoke of charring meat, in front of many restaurants during your stay. Other than traditional sardines, Portuguese grilled chicken -- marinated in chilli, garlic and olive oil -- is world famous, althou…

response.text:
See:
Lisbon is a city on the water—the River Tagus (Rio Tejo)—built on seven hills that are traversed by trams. This has led to comparisons with San Francisco. To provide access from the southern suburbs, Lisbon has two spectacular bridges. The 25th of April Bridge (Ponte 25 de Abril) combines the design of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge with the color of the Golden Gate Bridge, and it's often mistaken for the latter. The Vasco da Gama Bridge (Ponte Vasco da Gama), Europe's longest, was built in the 1990s for Expo '98. One of Lisbon's great landmarks, Cristo Rei, a 28 m statue of Christ the King on an 82 m pedestal, isn't even in Lisbon itself, but across the river in Almada, big enough to be easily seen from the capital.

Alfama:
Built on the hills east of the Baixa, Alfama survived the Great 1755 Earthquake largely intact. Climbing the narrow ancient lanes provides an excellent workout. You can spare your legs by taking the little historic yellow trams that serve the neighborhood. Major sights include Lisbon Cathedral and St. George's Castle.

Bairro Alto:
The Bairro Alto, or "Upper District" (dare we say "High Neighbourhood"), has become Lisbon's youthful, trendy quarter. The district includes the Chiado neighbourhood, known for its numerous historic landmarks and theatres. Among the district's many sights are the São Bento Palace (where the Portuguese parliament meets), the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (a museum of antique art), and the Lisbon Botanical Gardens.

response.text:
Eat:
Portuguese dining rituals tend to follow the Mediterranean siesta body clock. Most restaurants are very small, family-run and generally inexpensive. Some of them have a sheet on the door with the pratos do dia (dishes of the day) written on it – these dishes are usually cheaper and fresher than the rest of menu there, and unless you're looking for something specific, they're the right choice. During the dinner the waiter will probably bring you some unrequested starter dishes (called couvert); as those are not free, don't feel obliged to touch them and they will not be charged on your bill (but check it!).

Traditional Portuguese restaurants are in Bairro Alto, scattered abundantly through its quirky narrow streets, and for Portuguese traditional cuisine at its finest, head to the area of Chiado. Tour groups primarily feel at home in Alfama. Tourist traps with laminated menus and meal deals are mostly concentrated in the Baixa area; one exception to this is the Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, a 'seafood strip' northeast from and parallel to Praça dos Restauradores. If you feel like eating with the local people, try the Castelo neighborhood, the smaller family run places serve a fixed daily menu and are not expensive, getting up there by foot will open an appetite, or else go in the elétrico. For a familiar taste at one of the many chain eateries, head to Doca de Santo Amaro (train/tram 15 station Alcantara-Mar) and Parque das Nações (metro Oriental). All the culinary and …

results.name: Leitaria Camponeza
results.summary: On the location of a historical café (the leitaria), this place focuses on only a short number of dishes (meats, fish and seafood) but makes up for this in quality and portion size. For an atmospheric presentation ask for one of their espetadas. The wines complement the dishes and you can end the meal with a dessert. For someone looking for great value for their buck (no compromises on quality), it's a good place to start or end an evening. Price: €15-30

results.name: Mercado da Praça da Figueira
results.summary: From the pavement looks like a small convenience shop, on walking in you realize the deception when confronted by the large cavernous meandering interior space, replete with everything expected from a well stocked supermarket. Although there isn't a restaurant as such, the ready to eat items on offer are tasty, fresh, inexpensive and varied. The sandwiches and hamburgers are superb.

results.name: Mercado Oriental
results.summary: A food court serving Asian street food and the only place in Lisbon where you can try Macanese cuisine (at a stall called "Taberna Macau"). Price: Small dishes €3

results.name: Néctar WineBar
results.summary: A place dedicated to the promotion of Portugal's wine and gastronomic culture, and featuring a daily lunch menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine. The wine list comprises – in its vast majority – a selection of Portuguese wines which best represent the country. Wine can be bought by the glass, and it is served at the appropriate temperatures and in suitable glasses. Dishes – served in portions for 2 – easily replace a main course meal. results.title: São Jorge Castle
results.extract: São Jorge Castle (Portuguese: Castelo de São Jorge; Portuguese pronunciation: [kɐʃˈtɛlu dɨ sɐ̃w̃ ˈʒɔɾʒɨ]), sometimes known in English as Saint George's Castle, is a historic castle in the Portuguese capital of Lisbon, located in the freguesia of Santa Maria Maior. Human occupation of the castle hill dates to at least the 8th century BC while the oldest fortifications on the site date from the 2nd century BC. The hill on which Saint George's Castle stands has played an important part in the history of Lisbon, having served as the location of fortifications occupied successively by Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors, before its conquest by the Portuguese in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon. Since the 12th century, the castle has variously served as a royal palace, a military barracks, home of the Torre do Tombo National Archive, and now as a national monument and museum.

results.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
results.summary: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

results.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
results.summary: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little further out than the viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol, so it is usually quieter, and it is a fine place to watch the sunset.

results.name: Castelo de São Jorge
results.summary: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of the former Royal Palace of Alcáçova, a garden with native forest species, and a camera obscura showing the city's sights. The castle offers great view over the city and the river. I

results.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
results.summary: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.

results.name: Lisbon Cathedral
results.summary: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910. Price: , children 7–12 , children 6 & under free

results.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
results.summary: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor. Price: , seniors 65+/students/youth card , disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
results.summary: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

results.name: Museu de Sociedade de Geografia
results.summary: Exhibits of ethnography from Portugal's former colonies. Price: , seniors 65+ , students & youths , families of 4 or more  each, disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
results.summary: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

results.name: Panteão Nacional
results.summary: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the dome was added in 1966 and then converted to the National Pantheon. Amália Rodrigues, queen of fado, is buried here, and fresh roses can be seen on the tomb. The church also has wide viewing platform on the rooftop all around its dome. Excellent panorama of the river and surroundings. No elevator.
results.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, platform 10:00-18:00 (closed Mondays, shorter hours in winter)

response.answer: Bacalhau à brás is a traditional Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, onions, and thinly fried potato matchsticks, all bound with eggs. The dish is usually garnished with black olives and fresh cilantro or parsley. The main ingredients include salt cod, potatoes, eggs, and onion. The origin of the recipe is uncertain, but it is said to have originated in the late 19th century in Bairro Alto, Lisbon. The name "à brás" is believed to come from a 19th-century Lisbon tavern or restaurant called Braz. The dish is typically served with a side of boiled or steamed veggies or a fresh salad, crusty bread, and a dry white wine like Vinho verde.

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki on a mid‑budget (€2 500 total) who love history and street food. The weather information is based on typical conditions for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back
**Chosen outbound**: SAS flight, 11:15 → 16:10, 1 stop, 415 min, €297 (live) – [details](https://kiwi.com/u/jwhvkp)

**Chosen return**: Finnair flight, 16:35 → 23:10, non‑stop, 275 min, €387 (live) – [details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32)

### Outbound alternatives
|   | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price (all travellers) | Link |
|---|------|----------|----------------|----------|-------|------------------------|------|
| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, easyJet | 2027-05-10 23:15 → 2027-05-11 09:55 | 760 min | 1 | €293 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/fg5t4x3) |
| Fastest | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-10 13:00 → 2027-05-10 15:50 | 290 min | 0 | €411 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh) |
> **Note**: cheapest outbound requires an airport change (STN → LTN) and a self‑transfer.

### Return alternatives
|   | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price (all travellers) | Link |
|---|------|----------|----------------|----------|-------|------------------------|------|
| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, SAS | 2027-05-14 06:50 → 2027-05-14 20:25 | 695 min | 2 | €283 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26) |
| Fastest | flight | Finnair (chosen) | 2027-05-14 16:35 → 2027-05-14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |
> **Note**: cheapest return also involves airport changes.

## Where to stay
**Chosen stay**: [Marta's House](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/9152658?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) – Airbnb, 1 bedroom, 1 double bed, 1 bath, 1.1 km from centre, €89 / night, total €356 (live), rating 4.86/5. Best‑value mid‑budget option with good rating and central location.

> **Caveats**: liteAPI hotel rates may be 15‑30 % below public prices and exclude city tax. Airbnb taxes (€32) are already included in the total.

## Day by day
### Day 1 – Mon 2027-05-10: Baixa/Alfama
*Weather*: light rain – 0.7 km walk
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – flight with SAS. [source](https://kiwi.com/u/jwhvkp)
- **17:00 São Jorge Castle** – historic hilltop fortress occupied since the 8th century BC, later a royal palace and military barracks. Open Mo‑Su 09:00‑21:00. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Jorge_Castle)
- **18:00 Lisbon Cathedral** – Portugal's oldest church, founded 1147 after the Reconquest; mix of Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque. Open Mon‑Sat 10:00‑18:30. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama)
- **21:00 Néctar WineBar** – dinner, try a Portuguese classic (e.g., bacalhau) with a good wine pairing. Mid‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027-05-11: Belém
*Weather*: drizzle – 18.5 km walk
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – Manueline masterpiece, UNESCO World Heritage, founded by King Manuel I to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:30 (Oct‑May) / 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). ticket €18. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **12:45 Mercado Oriental** – lunch, Asian street bites and the famous Macanese stall; small dishes €3. Low‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **14:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – commemorates the Age of Discovery, 1960 caravel‑shaped monument; climb for Tagus views. ticket €4. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – dinner, traditional Portuguese dishes with an Indian twist; try the seafood rice. Mid‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 3 – Wed 2027-05-12: Alfama/Chiado
*Weather*: rain – 1.1 km walk
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – interactive exhibits on Portuguese sport history. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:00. free entry. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **12:15 Cervejaria da Trindade** – lunch, codfish plates and house‑brew beer. Mid‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:00 Monumento aos Restauradores** – commemorates the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. No ticket. [source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **19:30 Faca & Garfo** – dinner, grilled sardines or fish; mains €6‑8. Mid‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027-05-13: Chiado
*Weather*: drizzle – 2.6 km walk
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – modern Portuguese and international art; plan a 2‑hour visit. Open Tu‑Su 10:00‑18:00. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **13:00 Os Tibetanos** – lunch, vegan‑friendly dishes, light and healthy. Mid‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **19:30 Belcanto** – special dinner, two‑Michelin‑star tasting menu. High‑budget. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027-05-14: Parque das Nações
*Weather*: overcast – 2.3 km walk
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – world‑class collection spanning antiquities to modern art. Open Su‑Mo, We‑Fr 10:00‑18:00; Sa 10:00‑21:00. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calouste_Gulbenkian_Museum)
- **12:30 Restaurante Tascardoso** – lunch, simple affordable Portuguese dishes; standing‑room only, small dishes €3. High‑budget label. [source]()
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – flight with Finnair. [source](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32)

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg‑tart pastry dusted with cinnamon. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)
- **Feijoada** – bean and meat stew popular in Portuguese‑speaking areas. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q878189)
- **Francesinha** – Portuguese sandwich. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q732)
- **Fios de ovos** – Portuguese egg dessert. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3275692)
- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese stew. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki to Lisbon for a relaxed five‑day stay. The budget is mid‑range with a total of **€2500**. Interests are history and street food. Weather information is based on typical conditions for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back
**Chosen flights** are shown first, followed by the cheapest and fastest alternatives.

### Outbound (Helsinki → Lisbon)

| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, easyJet | 2027-05-10 23:15 → 2027-05-11 09:55 | 760 min | 1 | €293 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/fg5t4x3) |

### Return (Lisbon → Helsinki)

|--------|------|----------|----------------|----------|-------|------------------------|------|

| Fastest | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-14 16:35 → 2027-05-14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Notes:**

- All return flights include two personal items per traveller; no checked bags.

## Where to stay

### Day 1 – Mon 2027-05-10: Alfama/Baixa
*Weather:* light rain, 13‑17 °C — **walk 0.7 km**
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS; see Getting there and back.
- **17:00 São Jorge Castle** – Historic fortress overlooking the city; human occupation dates back to the 8th century BC and it later served as a royal palace. Hours 09:00‑21:00. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.castelodesaojorge.pt/)
- **18:00 Lisbon Cathedral** – The oldest church in Lisbon, founded in 1147 after the reconquest from the Moors; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Hours 10:00‑18:30. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **19:30 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑range wine bar; try the codfish dish and a house dessert. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027-05-11: Belém
*Weather:* drizzle, 13‑18 °C — **walk 7.0 km**
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO‑listed Manueline masterpiece built in the 16th century; founded by King Manuel I to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage. Hours 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). ticket €18. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **12:00 Monument to the Discoveries** – 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow, commemorating Portugal’s Age of Discovery. Climb the platform for river views. ticket €4. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Street‑food market with Asian stalls; try the small dishes (≈ €3). Budget low. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **18:30 Dinner near hotel** – Self‑catered, relaxed evening.

### Day 3 – Wed 2027-05-12: Alfama/Restauradores
*Weather:* rain, 13‑19 °C — **walk 0.8 km**
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Museum chronicling Portuguese sport history; free entry. Hours 10:00‑17:00 (Tu‑Su). [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **11:30 Monumento aos Restauradores** – Monument commemorating the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **13:00 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Restaurant‑brewery in a former monastery; try the grilled sardines and house‑brew beer. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **15:00 Museu Nacional do Azulejo** – Museum of Portuguese tiles from the 15th century to today, housed in the former Madre de Deus Convent. Indoor, great for rainy weather. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Three‑course dinner mixing Portuguese, Indian and Cape Verdean flavours. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027-05-13: Chiado
*Weather:* drizzle, 13‑19 °C — **walk 0.5 km**
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Modern art collection of Portuguese and international works. Hours 10:00‑18:00 (Tu‑Su). ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **13:00 Faca & Garfo** – Cozy spot; try the grilled sardines. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **19:00 Café Buenos Aires** – South‑American grill; sample the steak sandwich. Budget high. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027-05-14: Eduardo VII/Parque
*Weather:* overcast, 13‑20 °C — **walk 1.9 km**
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collection spanning antiquities to modern art, housed in a purpose‑built building. Hours 10:00‑18:00 (Su‑Mo, We‑Fr). ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/188143627)
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Vegetarian restaurant; try the tofu noodles. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair; see Getting there and back.

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg tart pastry dusted with cinnamon. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki to Lisbon for a relaxed five‑day stay. The budget is mid‑range with a total of **€2500**. Interests are history and street food. Weather information is based on typical conditions for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back
**Chosen flights** are shown first, followed by the cheapest and fastest alternatives.

### Outbound (Helsinki → Lisbon)

**Notes:**
- The cheapest outbound involves an airport change in London (STN → LTN) and requires a self‑transfer. 
- All flights include two personal items per traveller; no checked bags.

### Return (Lisbon → Helsinki)

| Cheapest | flight | Ryanair, SAS | 2027-05-14 06:50 → 2027-05-14 20:25 | 695 min | 2 | €283 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26) |
| Fastest | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-14 16:35 → 2027-05-14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Notes:**
- The cheapest return also needs two airport changes (Lisbon → AGP → ARN → HEL). 
- All return flights include two personal items per traveller; no checked bags.

## Where to stay
**Chosen accommodation:** [Green View Home](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Green+View+Home%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) – 3★ hotel, rating 4.1/5, free Wi‑Fi, some rooms with kitchen. €44 per night (live), total €176 (live) for 4 nights. Cheapest suitable lodging, leaving more budget for food and activities.

### Stay options by area

| Other | – | [Green View Home](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Green+View+Home%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) | €44 |

| Lisbon | [Double Bedroom with TV, Pool, and Private Bathroom](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/1457105680391230136?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) | – | €58 |
| Rua Aurea, 266 | – | [Rossio Plaza Hotel](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Rossio+Plaza+Hotel%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) | €109.44 |

**Caveats:**
- liteAPI hotel rates (Rossio Plaza, HF Fénix Urban) may be 15‑30 % lower than public booking sites and exclude city tax (e.g., €32.59 for Rossio Plaza). 
- No Airbnb fees or taxes are shown; check the booking page for final cost.

## Day by day
*Days in this plan start around 09:30 and end by 22:00, at a relaxed pace. For another rhythm, tell the concierge, e.g. "we wake up early, start at 07:00", "we stay out late" or "a more relaxed pace, please".*

### Day 1 – Mon 2027-05-10: Alfama/Baixa
*Weather:* light rain, 13‑17 °C — **walk 0.7 km**
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS; see Getting there and back.
- **17:00 São Jorge Castle** – Historic fortress overlooking the city; human occupation dates back to the 8th century BC and it later served as a royal palace. Hours 09:00‑21:00. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.castelodesaojorge.pt/)
- **18:00 Lisbon Cathedral** – The oldest church in Lisbon, founded in 1147 after the reconquest from the Moors; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Hours 10:00‑18:30. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **19:30 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑range wine bar; try the codfish dish and a house dessert. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027-05-11: Belém
*Weather:* drizzle, 13‑18 °C — **walk 7.0 km**
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO‑listed Manueline masterpiece built in the 16th century; founded by King Manuel I to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage. Hours 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). ticket €18. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **12:00 Monument to the Discoveries** – 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow, commemorating Portugal’s Age of Discovery. Climb the platform for river views. ticket €4. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Street‑food market with Asian stalls; try the small dishes (≈ €3). Budget low. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **18:30 Dinner near hotel** – Self‑catered, relaxed evening.

### Day 3 – Wed 2027-05-12: Alfama/Restauradores
*Weather:* rain, 13‑19 °C — **walk 0.8 km**
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Museum chronicling Portuguese sport history; free entry. Hours 10:00‑17:00 (Tu‑Su). [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **11:30 Monumento aos Restauradores** – Monument commemorating the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **13:00 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Restaurant‑brewery in a former monastery; try the grilled sardines and house‑brew beer. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **15:00 Museu Nacional do Azulejo** – Museum of Portuguese tiles from the 15th century to today, housed in the former Madre de Deus Convent. Indoor, great for rainy weather. ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Three‑course dinner mixing Portuguese, Indian and Cape Verdean flavours. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027-05-13: Chiado
*Weather:* drizzle, 13‑19 °C — **walk 0.5 km**
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Modern art collection of Portuguese and international works. Hours 10:00‑18:00 (Tu‑Su). ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **13:00 Faca & Garfo** – Cozy spot; try the grilled sardines. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **19:00 Café Buenos Aires** – South‑American grill; sample the steak sandwich. Budget high. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027-05-14: Eduardo VII/Parque
*Weather:* overcast, 13‑20 °C — **walk 1.9 km**
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collection spanning antiquities to modern art, housed in a purpose‑built building. Hours 10:00‑18:00 (Su‑Mo, We‑Fr). ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/188143627)
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Vegetarian restaurant; try the tofu noodles. Budget mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair; see Getting there and back.

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg tart pastry dusted with cinnamon. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)
- **Feijoada** – Bean and meat stew popular in Portuguese‑speaking areas. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q878189)
- **Francesinha** – Portuguese sandwich. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q732)
- **Fios de ovos** – Portuguese egg dessert. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3275692)
- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese stew. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

## Cost estimate
| Category | Total (€) | Share |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| Transport | 684.0 | 43.2% |
| Stay | 176.0 | 11.1% |
| Food | 600.0 | 37.9% |

| Local transport | 80.0 | 5.1% |
| **Total** | **1584.0** | 100% |

**Per person:** €792.0
**Per person per day:** €158.4
**Budget used:** 63.4 % (within budget)

**Assumptions:**
- Food: typical mid‑budget cost of €50 per person per day.
- Local transport: typical €8 per person per day.
- Extra €100 for planned restaurants above the mid budget (low €15, mid €30, high €80 per person).
- Six sights with unknown ticket prices counted as €0.

## Good to know
- No failed sources; all data retrieved successfully.
- Prices for flights and hotels should be double‑checked before booking (especially liteAPI hotel rates, which may exclude city tax).
- Some attractions are closed on certain days (e.g., Museu Nacional do Azulejo is closed on Mondays).
- No major events are listed for the travel dates.
- Before booking, check your government's official travel advice for Portugal (safety, entry rules, insurance).
